# CLAUDE.md — midap-tools

## Project Overview

**midap-tools** is a post-processing and analysis toolkit for microfluidic experiment data generated by [MIDAP](https://github.com/Microbial-Systems-Ecology/midap), a segmentation and tracking pipeline for time-lapse cell imaging. The library is designed primarily for Jupyter notebook workflows targeting microbial ecology researchers.

src/
├── fluid_experiment/

## Architecture

Three-layer design:

1. **Raw data layer** — MIDAP output on disk (CSV tracking files, HDF5 segmentation masks, image stacks). Never modified.
2. **FluidExperiment** — Central orchestration class. Holds all data in memory as a nested dict: `data[position][color_channel] = pd.DataFrame`. All operations are in-place on this structure.
3. **Analysis/Plotting layer** — Standalone, stateless functions that take DataFrames, return DataFrames or figures.

**Key principle:** raw data is never touched; all mutations live in memory and can be persisted via `experiment.save(path)` to HDF5.

## FluidExperiment Class

### Data structure
```python
experiment.data[position][channel]  # → pd.DataFrame
experiment.positions                 # list[str]
experiment.color_channels            # list[str]
experiment.metadata                  # pd.DataFrame | None
experiment.filter_history            # dict tracking all filters applied
```

### DataFrame columns — input (from MIDAP tracking files)
| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `globalID` | Unique row identifier across the full dataset |
| `frame` | Time index (int, 0-based) |
| `labelID` | Segmentation label ID within a single frame |
| `trackID` | Cell track identifier (unique per lineage branch) |
| `lineageID` | Lineage group identifier (shared across a cell family) |
| `trackID_d1` | trackID of first daughter cell after division |
| `trackID_d2` | trackID of second daughter cell after division |
| `split` | Frame index at which this cell divides (0 if no split) |
| `trackID_mother` | trackID of the mother cell this track originated from |
| `first_frame` | First frame in which this trackID appears |
| `last_frame` | Last frame in which this trackID appears |
| `area` | Cell area in pixels |
| `edges_min_row` | Bounding box top row |
| `edges_min_col` | Bounding box left column |
| `edges_max_row` | Bounding box bottom row |
| `edges_max_col` | Bounding box right column |
| `intensity_max` | Maximum pixel intensity within the cell mask |
| `intensity_mean` | Mean pixel intensity within the cell mask |
| `intensity_min` | Minimum pixel intensity within the cell mask |
| `minor_axis_length` | Minor axis length of the fitted ellipse (pixels) |
| `major_axis_length` | Major axis length of the fitted ellipse (pixels) |
| `x` | Cell centroid x-coordinate (column direction, float) |
| `y` | Cell centroid y-coordinate (row direction, float) |

### DataFrame columns — added by midap-tools
| Column | Added by |
|--------|---------|
| `growth_rate` | `calculate_growth_rate()` |
| `density_<channel>` | `calculate_local_neighborhood()` |
| `<col>_smoothed` | `smooth_data()` |

### Method categories

| Category | Methods |
|----------|---------|
| Loading | `__init__`, `load`, `from_copy` |
| Saving | `save` |
| Filtering | `filter_data`, `filter_segment_shape`, `clear_filter_history` |

## Conventions to Follow

### Updating the class docstring
Every new `FluidExperiment` method must be added to the `Methods:` section of the class docstring in `fluid_experiment.py`, in the same logical group as related methods (loading, filtering, calculation, plotting, reporting). Use the same one-line summary style as existing entries.

### Adding a new analysis method
1. Write the pure computation in `src/analysis/<module>.py` — takes a DataFrame (and supporting args), returns a DataFrame with new columns added.
2. Wire it into `FluidExperiment` in `fluid_experiment.py` following the existing pattern:
   - Iterate over `self.positions` and `self.color_channels`
   - Call the module function per (position, channel) pair
   - Assign result back: `self.data[pos][ch] = result_df`
   - Accept `custom_function` + `**custom_kwargs` for user extensibility

### Adding a new plot method
1. Write the plotting function in `src/plotting/<module>.py` — takes DataFrame(s), returns a matplotlib/plotnine figure.
2. Expose it on `FluidExperiment` as a thin wrapper that collects the relevant DataFrames and calls the function.

### Adding a new mutation/filter
1. Implement in `src/mutate/<module>.py`.
2. Return a summary dict `{"before": n, "after": m, ...}` for filter operations so the caller can update `filter_history`.

### Extensibility pattern
Most `FluidExperiment` methods accept a `custom_function` argument. The utility `_call_custom_filter()` in `utilities.py` uses introspection to bind only the parameters the custom function declares — follow this pattern when adding new customizable methods.

### Position/channel argument handling
Use `_save_select()` (defined in `fluid_experiment.py`) to normalize single strings to lists before iterating, so callers can pass either `"CFP"` or `["CFP", "YFP"]`.

### Naming
- New analysis columns: `<descriptive_name>` (no underscores prefix, avoid generic names)
- Smoothed variants: `<column>_smoothed`
- Module-level functions: `snake_case`
- Class methods: `snake_case`, verb-first (`calculate_`, `plot_`, `filter_`, `render_`)

## Key Dependencies
- **Data**: pandas, numpy, h5py
- **Image processing**: opencv-python, scikit-image, PIL
- **Visualization**: matplotlib, plotnine, seaborn, imageio
- **Statistics**: scipy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, scikit-misc
- **Notebooks**: jupyterlab

## Testing
Tests mirror the `src/` layout under `tests/`. Run with pytest. When adding a new function in `src/analysis/` or `src/mutate/`, add a corresponding test file.
